title: Fu Manchu
paragraphs: Serialized radio adaptations of Sax Rohmer's Fu Manchu stories, following the struggle of Nayland Smith and Dr. Petrie against the schemes of the brilliant and dangerous criminal mastermind.
Frozen GRH collection is the 1939 transcribed/syndicated Shadow of Fu Manchu serial, not the separate 1932 CBS series. It adapts Sax Rohmer novels in continuing 15-minute chapters.
GRH documents the program through 1939 Radio Attractions serial slice (May 8, 1939 to November 4, 1939).

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Hanley Stafford (performer on 73 recordings), [[person|gale-gordon|Gale Gordon]] (performer on 64 recordings and announcer on 3 recordings), [[person|gerald-mohr|Gerald Mohr]] (announcer on 43 recordings and performer on 7 recordings), Lou Marcelle (performer on 16 recordings), Paula Winslowe (performer on 4 recordings), [[person|edmond-obrien|Edmond O’Brien]] (performer on 1 recording), and [[person|howard-mcnear|Howard McNear]] (performer on 1 recording).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.8b1104e3b833338e|Radio Attractions]] (syndicated by).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include international and colonial settings, secret societies and hidden networks, murder and attempted murder, science used as a threat or weapon, abduction and captivity, and poisons and exotic toxins.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Transcription syndication through Radio Attractions, Sax Rohmer novel-to-radio serial adaptation, Fu Manchu and Yellow Peril popular imagery, and Interwar serial cliffhanger culture.

plain_text:
Serialized radio adaptations of Sax Rohmer's Fu Manchu stories, following the struggle of Nayland Smith and Dr. Petrie against the schemes of the brilliant and dangerous criminal mastermind.

Frozen GRH collection is the 1939 transcribed/syndicated Shadow of Fu Manchu serial, not the separate 1932 CBS series. It adapts Sax Rohmer novels in continuing 15-minute chapters.

GRH documents the program through 1939 Radio Attractions serial slice (May 8, 1939 to November 4, 1939).

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Hanley Stafford (performer on 73 recordings), Gale Gordon (performer on 64 recordings and announcer on 3 recordings), Gerald Mohr (announcer on 43 recordings and performer on 7 recordings), Lou Marcelle (performer on 16 recordings), Paula Winslowe (performer on 4 recordings), Edmond O’Brien (performer on 1 recording), and Howard McNear (performer on 1 recording).

The program is also connected in the archive to Radio Attractions (syndicated by).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include international and colonial settings, secret societies and hidden networks, murder and attempted murder, science used as a threat or weapon, abduction and captivity, and poisons and exotic toxins.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Transcription syndication through Radio Attractions, Sax Rohmer novel-to-radio serial adaptation, Fu Manchu and Yellow Peril popular imagery, and Interwar serial cliffhanger culture.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include Lux Radio Theatre (6 shared credited people), Escape (5 shared credited people), The Railroad Hour (5 shared credited people), Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar (5 shared credited people), and Broadway Is My Beat (4 shared credited people).
